scope: Permit gz02 Linux x86_64 compilation into project-owned OUT and bounded --probe plus ordinary exec positive/negative tests using inert commands only. No Soong graph, target build, container, namespace launcher or device execution.

static_checks.bpf_control_flow: Architecture mismatch kills; AUDIT_ARCH_X86_64 continues. x32 syscall bit kills. Equality macros deny unshare, setns, chroot, pivot_root and mount-family syscalls. clone3 returns ENOSYS because classic BPF cannot dereference its flags pointer. clone checks low 32-bit arg0 flags on x86_64 and denies any NEW_NAMESPACE_FLAGS bit; non-clone and ordinary clone fall through to allow. Branch offsets statically consistent.
static_checks.host_abi: GZ02 Linux 6.8.0-87-generic x86_64. Host unistd_64.h defines clone3 and all optional mount API syscall numbers; linux/sched.h defines all eight listed CLONE_NEW* flags. Source now rejects __ILP32__ x32 compilation. Historical pre-5.4 x32 nr 512-547 caveat is outside this pinned host scope.
static_checks.probe_safety: unshare(0) is a no-op without filter; chroot and mount receive invalid pointers; clone3(NULL,0) is invalid; clone uses CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_THREAD, an invalid flag combination. Thus if the filter is wrong, probe cannot perform the former real user namespace creation or mount tmpfs over root. It expects filter-specific EPERM/ENOSYS and fails closed otherwise.
static_checks.error_paths: PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS or PR_SET_SECCOMP failure returns 70 before probe/exec; execvp failure returns 71. Filter is installed before execvp and inherited through permitted fork/clone/exec descendants.

conditions: Compile exact reviewed source SHA into gz02 project OUT, recording compiler argv/rc and resulting ELF SHA. Do not compile into shared source or Bridge paths.
Run --probe only on the built exact binary; record actual exit code, stdout/stderr and bounded process trace.
Ordinary exec positives may use inert commands such as /usr/bin/true; negatives must use nonexistent executable or harmless invalid-argument helpers, never a live namespace/mount/container launcher.
A successful probe is a filter smoke test, not Soong graph release. Separately review runner argv and generated actions before any graph command.
limitations: The generic execvp interface can launch arbitrary commands, including clients that talk to an external daemon; the caller must pin allowed argv. Seccomp is not a complete container prohibition or sandbox.
The #ifdef guards for clone3 and newer mount syscalls depend on build headers; GO is limited to the observed gz02 headers and must fail if compiler/header identity differs.
Probe does not exercise every denied syscall; static branch review and future bounded tests remain separate.
